title: Review a disposition schedule and resolve Form 4797 diagnostics — Ellis Fabrication
instructions: Rae Ellis operates Ellis Fabrication as a sole proprietorship. A staff member prepared the 2025 disposition schedule for Form 4797 and Form 8824. Review it, resolve the software diagnostics, then compute the replacement basis. Tick every amount that is wrong and enter the correct amount. Enter losses as negative numbers.

exhibits.title: 2025 dispositions
exhibits.content:
| Asset | Held | Cost | Accumulated depreciation | Amount realized |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Equipment A | 4 years | 80,000 | 50,000 | 45,000 |
| Equipment B | 3 years | 60,000 | 20,000 | 70,000 |
| Building (nonresidential, straight-line) | 9 years | 500,000 | 120,000 | 450,000 |
| Land (parking lot) | 5 years | 90,000 | — | 75,000 |
| Truck | 8 months | 40,000 | 6,000 | 30,000 |

**Exchange:** Rae exchanged business land (basis **$120,000**, FMV **$200,000**, held 6 years) for other business land (FMV **$180,000**) plus **$20,000** cash.

Rae had no §1231 losses in the prior five years.

rows.label: Equipment A — ordinary gain (§1245 recapture)
rows.explanation: Gain 45,000 − (80,000 − 50,000) = 15,000, all recapture because depreciation (50,000) exceeds the gain. **No error.**

rows.label: Equipment B — ordinary gain (§1245 recapture)
rows.explanation: Gain 70,000 − 40,000 = 30,000. Recapture is the lesser of the gain or the depreciation taken: **20,000** ordinary.

rows.label: Equipment B — §1231 gain
rows.explanation: Only the gain above the depreciation taken is §1231: 30,000 − 20,000 = **10,000**.

rows.label: Building — §1231 gain
rows.explanation: 450,000 − 380,000 = 70,000. Straight-line depreciation leaves no §1250 ordinary recapture. **No error.**

rows.label: Truck — ordinary loss (Form 4797 Part II)
rows.explanation: Held only 8 months, so it is **not** §1231 property: the 4,000 loss is ordinary.

rows.label: Land exchange — recognized gain
rows.explanation: Realized gain 80,000, recognized only to the extent of the **20,000** cash boot (§1031(b)). The rest is deferred.

rows.label: Net §1231 gain
rows.explanation: 10,000 + 70,000 − 15,000 + 20,000 = **85,000**. The truck is excluded. There are no nonrecaptured §1231 losses from prior years, so the full amount is long-term capital gain.

rows.label: Unrecaptured §1250 gain (25% rate)
rows.explanation: The lesser of the straight-line depreciation on the building (120,000) and its gain (70,000). **No error.**

parts.prompt: Choose the correct resolution for each diagnostic.

rows.label: Form 8824: delivery van exchanged for a new van reported as a like-kind exchange.
options: Report it as a taxable sale — §1031 now applies only to real property
Report it as an involuntary conversion
rows.answer: Report it as a taxable sale — §1031 now applies only to real property
rows.explanation: Since 2018 like-kind treatment is limited to real property not held primarily for sale.

rows.label: An asset held one year or less is reported in Form 4797 Part I.
options: Move it to Part II (ordinary gain or loss)
rows.answer: Move it to Part II (ordinary gain or loss)
rows.explanation: §1231 requires a holding period of more than one year.

rows.label: Depreciation was allowed on Equipment B but no recapture is reported.
options: Clear the flag — the gain is all §1231
Report the recapture as a capital gain
rows.explanation: Gain up to prior depreciation on personal property is ordinary.

rows.label: Form 8824: cash received in a land-for-land exchange.
options: Recognize gain up to the cash received
rows.answer: Recognize gain up to the cash received
rows.explanation: Boot triggers gain up to the lesser of the boot or the realized gain.

parts.prompt: Compute the basis of the replacement land.

rows.label: Basis of the land received
rows.explanation: Old basis 120,000 + gain recognized 20,000 − cash received 20,000 = **120,000** (FMV 180,000 − deferred gain 60,000).
